behavior_constraints: schema command auto-infers JSON schema from CSV via --input/--output flags
Type detection uses strconv.ParseInt (base 10, 64-bit) then strconv.ParseFloat (64-bit), else string
required is true only when no empty values exist in the column and total_rows > 0
unique is true only when all non-empty values are distinct and at least one non-empty value exists
min/max included only for int/float types with non-empty values, as actual numeric values
enum included only for string type with 10 or fewer unique non-empty values, sorted alphabetically
Each column constraint object always includes type; required/unique/min/max/enum included only when applicable
Column keys in columns map are sorted alphabetically (encoding/json default)
Output is 2-space indented JSON with trailing newline
entities.summary: This round adds a schema command that auto-infers JSON schemas from CSV, a mask transform for sensitive data, a pipeline schema step, and lineage recognition of schema steps.

instruction_head:
Add the following capabilities to `dpipe`.

## New command: `schema`

`dpipe schema --input <path> --output <path>`

Auto-infers a JSON schema from CSV data. For each column, analyze all data rows:

- **Type detection**: same logic as quality command. Try `strconv.ParseInt` (base 10, 64-bit) on all non-empty values. If all succeed, type is `"int"`. Else try `strconv.ParseFloat` (64-bit) on all. If all succeed, type is `"float"`. Else type is `"string"`.
